decisions.reason: Because Product A builds directly on the firm's established laser marking knowledge and in-house R&D, the firm can interpret its early results and improve it, making withdrawal unlikely.
Because Product B is close to existing thermal inkjet and coding technologies, the firm has the absorptive capacity to learn from market feedback and further develop it.
Because Product C leverages the firm's related piezo inkjet know-how and internal R&D, it can assimilate early performance data and apply improvements, making a drop improbable.

As a flagship industrial laser line that extends the firm's core marking knowledge, Product D aligns with strategic direction and benefits from high absorptive capacity, so withdrawal is very unlikely.
Because Product E is a compact laser cabin that builds on established laser marking competencies, the firm can evaluate its market introduction and refine it, making a drop unlikely.

Although Product F applies printing to a newer lubricant-on-sheet-metal context, its award and closeness to the firm's high-resolution coding capabilities enable the firm to learn and improve it, so it will likely be kept.
